breakfast.name: Bojo (Cassava Cake)
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C and grease a baking dish.
Squeeze excess moisture from the grated cassava using a clean cloth.
Mix cassava with grated coconut, sugar, melted butter, eggs, vanilla, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Add evaporated milk and stir until well combined.
Pour into the greased baking dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden brown and set.
Let cool before slicing into squares.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
breakfast.description: A sweet, dense cassava and coconut cake that reflects Suriname's Javanese and Creole heritage. Often enjoyed at breakfast or as a snack.

breakfast.name: Broodje Bakkeljauw (Salt Cod Sandwich)
ingredients: 300g salt cod, soaked overnight and drained
1 Madame Jeanette pepper, seeded and sliced
instructions: Shred the soaked salt cod and remove any bones.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the cod with onion and pepper until lightly golden.
Squeeze lime juice over the cod mixture.
Slice the bread rolls in half.
Layer lettuce, tomato slices, cucumber, and the warm cod mixture on each roll.
Serve immediately as a hearty breakfast sandwich.
breakfast.description: Suriname's beloved street sandwich filled with flaked salt cod, spicy Madame Jeanette pepper, and fresh vegetables. Dutch colonial heritage meets Caribbean flavor.

breakfast.name: Bakabana (Fried Plantain with Peanut Sauce)
ingredients: Peanut sauce (peanut butter, water, sweet soy sauce, garlic, chilli)
instructions: Bakabana is the Surinamese fried plantain with peanut sauce
A street food combination unique to Suriname
The ripe plantain is fried until caramelized
Served with peanut sauce: a Surinamese-Dutch-Indonesian combination
The peanut sauce: Indonesian satay sauce influence
Suriname was Dutch colonial territory from 1667-1975
The Dutch brought Javanese contract laborers from Indonesia (1890s)
breakfast.description: Surinamese fried plantain with peanut sauce -- ripe caramelized plantain served with Indonesian-influenced peanut sauce (peanut butter, sweet soy sauce, chilli). Bakabana reflects the Surinamese fusion: Dutch colonization brought Javanese contract workers from Indonesia (1890s), embedding Indonesian flavors.

breakfast.name: Bara (Fried Dough)
instructions: Bara are the Surinamese fried dough balls
Similar to the Dominican-Caribbean version
A legacy of the diverse Surinamese population
Eaten for breakfast with coffee
Sometimes split and filled with homemade jam or condensed milk
breakfast.description: Surinamese fried dough balls -- lightly sweetened yeast dough deep-fried until golden. A simple, beloved breakfast from the diverse Surinamese street food tradition. Sometimes split and filled with jam or condensed milk.

lunch.name: Pom (Tayer Root Casserole)
instructions: Boil chicken thighs until cooked, about 25 minutes. Reserve the broth. Shred the meat.
Grate the tayer root and immediately mix with orange and lemon juice to prevent discoloration.
Heat oil and sauté onions and garlic. Add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix the sautéed onion mixture with the grated tayer, shredded chicken, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Add enough chicken broth to make the mixture moist but not watery.
Pour into a greased baking dish, dot with butter on top.
Bake at 180°C for 50-60 minutes until the top is golden and crispy.
Let rest 10 minutes before serving.
lunch.description: Suriname's most celebrated dish, a baked casserole of grated tayer root layered with chicken in citrus-spiced gravy. Essential at every family celebration.

lunch.name: Roti met Kip (Roti with Chicken Curry)
ingredients: For roti: 3 cups flour, 1 cup water, 2 tbsp butter, 1 tsp salt
instructions: Make the roti dough by mixing flour, salt, water, and butter. Knead until smooth, rest 30 minutes.
Heat oil and toast cumin seeds. Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Add masala powder and stir for 30 seconds. Add chicken and brown on all sides.
Add potatoes and coconut milk. Simmer for 30 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Divide roti dough into balls, roll out thin, brush with butter, fold, and roll again.
Cook each roti on a hot tawa until puffed and golden on both sides.
Clap the roti between your hands to make it flaky.
Serve the curry ladled over torn pieces of roti.
lunch.description: Flaky, layered flatbread served with fragrant chicken and potato curry. Suriname's Hindustani community brought this dish, and it became a national favorite.

lunch.name: Moksi Alesi (Mixed Rice)
ingredients: Creole spices: thyme, cumin, scotch bonnet
instructions: Moksi alesi means mixed rice in Sranan Tongo (the Surinamese Creole language)
A Creole one-pot rice dish with mixed protein and legumes
Black-eyed peas: the African culinary legacy in Suriname
African slaves were brought to Suriname (1600s-1800s) -- their food legacy is central
Sranan Tongo (also called Surinamese): the Creole lingua franca
The dish reflects the Afro-Surinamese contribution to the national cuisine
lunch.description: Surinamese mixed rice -- Afro-Surinamese one-pot rice (moksi = mixed in Sranan Tongo Creole language) with salted fish, chicken or shrimp, and black-eyed peas. African slaves brought to Suriname from the 1600s established the Afro-Surinamese culinary tradition that is central to the national cuisine.

lunch.name: Roti met Kerrie (Roti with Curry)
instructions: Surinamese roti is from the Hindustani (Indian) community
Hindustani: the term for Surinamese of Indian descent
Brought from India (1873-1916) as indentured workers to replace freed enslaved people
The Hindustani community brought: roti, curry, dal, and a distinct spice tradition
Surinamese roti is larger and softer than Trinidad roti -- an Antillean style
The curry is wrapped inside the roti for eating -- the roti is the vessel
lunch.description: Surinamese Indian-heritage roti with curry -- large, soft, layered roti (brought by Hindustani indentured workers from India, 1873-1916) wrapping a chicken or potato curry (Hindustani-style: South Indian spice profile with coconut milk). The Hindustani community is one of the largest Surinamese ethnic groups.

lunch.name: Bruine Bonen Soep (Brown Bean Soup)
instructions: Bruine bonen soep is the Dutch-Surinamese brown bean soup
A legacy of Dutch colonization -- brown bean soup is a Dutch staple
Adapted with Surinamese ingredients and spices
Smoked pork ribs for depth
Eaten on Sundays as a family meal
lunch.description: Surinamese brown bean soup -- Dutch colonial legacy, brown kidney beans simmered with smoked pork ribs and aromatics. Adapted from the Dutch split pea/bean soup tradition with Surinamese Creole spicing. Sunday family soup.

dinner.name: Moksi-Alesi (Mixed Rice)
ingredients: 200g salt pork or smoked chicken, diced
instructions: Heat oil and fry the salt pork or smoked chicken until crispy.
Add onion and garlic, sauté until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and diced tomato, cook for 2 minutes.
Add rice and stir to coat with the mixture.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth. Add the whole pepper and black-eyed peas.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for 20 minutes.
Remove pepper. Fluff with a fork.
Serve as a complete one-pot meal.
dinner.description: A hearty one-pot rice dish with meat, beans, and coconut milk that exemplifies Suriname's Creole kitchen. The Madame Jeanette pepper adds gentle heat.

dinner.name: Saoto Soup
instructions: Bring water to a boil with chicken, lemongrass, garlic, galangal, salam leaves, and turmeric.
Simmer for 40 minutes until the chicken is falling off the bone.
Remove chicken, shred the meat, and strain the broth.
In each serving bowl, place some steamed rice, glass noodles, bean sprouts, and shredded chicken.
Ladle the hot broth over the top.
Garnish with hard-boiled egg halves, fried shallots, and celery leaves.
Serve with sambal and kecap manis on the side.
dinner.description: A fragrant Javanese-Surinamese chicken soup with turmeric, lemongrass, and galangal, served over rice with noodles and bean sprouts.

dinner.name: Pom (Tayer Root Casserole)
ingredients: Tayer root (similar to taro -- the Surinamese-Jewish legacy vegetable)
instructions: Pom is one of Suriname most beloved and unique dishes
A casserole of grated tayer root (a type of taro) with chicken
The Surinamese Jewish community (from Brazil and Portugal, arriving 1600s) developed pom
The citrus juice: the Jewish dietary influence (not mixing dairy with meat, hence no cream)
The tayer root gives a starchy, slightly tannic base
The chicken melts into the root base
Pom is made for every Surinamese celebration: funerals, weddings, birthdays
dinner.description: Surinamese Jewish-heritage tayer root casserole -- grated tayer root (similar to taro) baked with chicken, citrus juice, and onions. Developed by the Surinamese Sephardic Jewish community (arrived from Brazil, 1600s). The citrus replaces cream (Jewish dietary laws). Made at every Surinamese celebration.

dinner.name: Nasi Goreng (Surinamese Fried Rice)
instructions: Nasi goreng is the Indonesian fried rice -- brought to Suriname by Javanese workers
Suriname has the largest Javanese diaspora outside Indonesia
The Javanese community (from Java, Indonesia) brought their full food tradition
Kecap manis: Indonesian sweet soy sauce -- the essential nasi goreng flavor
Sambal: the Indonesian chilli paste -- also in the dish
The Surinamese version is nearly identical to the Indonesian original
dinner.description: Surinamese Javanese fried rice -- nasi goreng brought by the Javanese community (Java, Indonesia; brought as indentured workers). Suriname has the largest Javanese diaspora outside Indonesia. Kecap manis (sweet soy sauce) and sambal (chilli paste) are the essential flavors. Nearly identical to the Indonesian original.

dinner.name: Fowru Doro (Javanese Chicken)
instructions: Fowru doro is a Surinamese-Javanese spiced chicken dish
Javanese spices: lemongrass, galangal, kecap manis, turmeric
A braise that slowly reduces the sauce
The kecap manis caramelizes as it reduces
Eaten with rice
dinner.description: Surinamese Javanese braised chicken -- chicken in Javanese spices (lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, coriander) with kecap manis (sweet soy sauce) that caramelizes as the braising liquid reduces. The Javanese spice tradition preserved in the Surinamese Javanese diaspora.

snacks.name: Bara (Fried Lentil Fritters)
ingredients: 1 cup yellow split peas, soaked 4 hours
instructions: Drain the soaked split peas and grind into a thick paste.
Mix in onion, garlic, cumin, turmeric, hot pepper, and salt.
Heat oil to 175°C.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil and flatten slightly.
Fry until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with tamarind chutney or peanut sauce.
snacks.description: Crispy fried lentil fritters spiced with cumin and hot pepper. A beloved Surinamese street snack from the Hindustani tradition.

snacks.name: Saoto Soup (Javanese Chicken Soup)
ingredients: Spice paste: shallot, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, turmeric, candlenut
instructions: Saoto is the Surinamese-Javanese chicken soup -- one of the most beloved
A clear spiced chicken broth
Toppings: bean sprouts, egg, fried potato pieces, spring onion
The broth is flavored with a Javanese spice paste
A complete meal in a bowl
Saoto soup has its own culture in Suriname: dedicated saoto soup stalls
snacks.description: Surinamese Javanese chicken soup -- clear spiced chicken broth (Javanese spice paste: galangal, lemongrass, turmeric, candlenut) with toppings: bean sprouts, hard-boiled egg, fried potato pieces, and spring onion. One of the most beloved Surinamese dishes with dedicated saoto stalls.

snacks.name: Cassava Cake
instructions: Cassava cake is the Afro-Surinamese baking tradition
Grated cassava baked with coconut milk into a dense, sweet cake
Cinnamon and vanilla spiced
Similar versions exist throughout the Afro-Caribbean world
snacks.description: Surinamese cassava cake -- grated cassava baked with coconut milk, sugar, and cinnamon into a dense sweet cake. Afro-Surinamese baking tradition shared across the Afro-Caribbean world.

snacks.name: Ketjap Noodles (Cold)
instructions: Cold noodles with kecap manis: a Javanese-Surinamese quick snack
The sweet soy sauce coats the cold noodles
Sambal for heat
Fried shallots for crunch
A quick, satisfying snack
snacks.description: Surinamese cold noodles with sweet soy sauce -- thin egg noodles dressed with kecap manis (Indonesian sweet soy), sambal, cucumber, and fried shallots. A quick Javanese-Surinamese snack.

desserts.name: Fiyadoe (Sponge Cake)
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C and grease a round cake pan.
Beat eggs and sugar until thick, pale, and tripled in volume.
Sift in flour and baking powder, folding gently.
Drizzle in melted butter, vanilla, almond extract, and lemon zest. Fold until combined.
Pour into the prepared pan.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving.
desserts.description: A light, airy Surinamese sponge cake with hints of almond and lemon. A staple at birthdays and Javanese celebrations.

desserts.name: Bolo Preto (Black Cake)
instructions: Bolo preto (black cake) is the Surinamese Christmas fruit cake
Related to the Caribbean black cake -- the colonial British connection
Fruit soaked in rum for weeks or months
The browning makes it almost black
Made weeks before Christmas and aged
Every Surinamese family recipe is unique
desserts.description: Surinamese Christmas black cake -- dried fruit soaked in rum for weeks, mixed with browning sauce (caramelized sugar for the almost-black color) and warm spices, baked dense and boozy. Related to Caribbean black cake: the Surinamese Christmas tradition. Made weeks ahead and aged.

desserts.name: Klepon (Javanese Rice Balls)
ingredients: Palm sugar filling (gula jawa -- Javanese brown sugar)
instructions: Klepon are the Javanese green glutinous rice balls -- brought to Suriname
The rice dough is colored green with pandan
Filled with a nugget of palm sugar
Boiled until they float
Rolled in fresh grated coconut
When bitten: the palm sugar dissolves and bursts out
desserts.description: Surinamese Javanese green rice balls -- pandan-green glutinous rice dough filled with palm sugar (gula jawa), boiled until floating, rolled in fresh coconut. When bitten, the palm sugar bursts. Klepon from the Javanese diaspora.

drinks.name: Dawet (Coconut Milk Drink)
instructions: Mix rice flour with water and pandan extract (and green coloring if using). Cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick.
Press the cooked mixture through a colander or cendol press into a bowl of ice water to form short, worm-like strands.
Make palm sugar syrup by melting grated palm sugar with water.
In tall glasses, layer the pandan jelly strands, crushed ice, coconut milk, and palm sugar syrup.
Stir gently before drinking.
Serve immediately.
drinks.description: A sweet, icy Javanese-Surinamese drink with pandan-flavored jelly strands swimming in coconut milk and palm sugar syrup.

drinks.name: Rum Punch Surinamese Style
instructions: Combine rum, pineapple juice, orange juice, passion fruit juice, and lime juice in a pitcher.
Add grenadine and stir well.
Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the punch over.
Garnish each glass with a pineapple slice.
Grate fresh nutmeg on top.
Serve chilled.
drinks.description: A tropical fruit punch made with Borgoe rum, Suriname's most famous spirit. Bursting with pineapple, passion fruit, and a dash of nutmeg.

drinks.name: Dawet (Javanese Sweet Drink)
ingredients: Pandan jelly noodles (made from rice flour and pandan juice)
instructions: Dawet is the Javanese dessert drink -- brought to Suriname
Pandan-green jelly noodles in cold coconut milk and palm sugar syrup
The combination: cool, sweet, fragrant
Sold at Surinamese Javanese markets
The palm sugar (gula jawa) is specifically Javanese -- dark, caramel, earthy
drinks.description: Surinamese Javanese dessert drink -- pandan-green jelly noodles in cold coconut milk with palm sugar syrup (gula jawa: Javanese dark palm sugar). From the Surinamese Javanese diaspora. Cool, sweet, and fragrant.
